extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or researchers in algebraic topology / differential topology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and proof of Poincaré duality for (possibly noncompact) R-orientable n-manifolds, including constructions (cap product), compactly supported cohomology, Mayer–Vietoris technical lemmas, and consequences for cup product and manifold invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs and fundamental class / orientability criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain ∑ i k_i σ_i (with each coefficient k_i = ±1) defines a cycle iff the signs k_i can be chosen compatibly so that whenever σ_i and σ_j share an (n−1)-face the signs determine each other; such a choice is possible exactly when M is orientable, and then the cycle defines a fundamental class. With Z2 coefficients the sign issue disappears and ∑ i σ_i always defines a fundamental class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how local sign-consistency for top-dimensional simplices encodes orientability; use Z2 coefficients to avoid sign issues. This is the concrete combinatorial condition for existence of a fundamental class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.28: torsion in H_{n-1}(M;Z)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a closed connected n-manifold, the torsion subgroup of H_{n-1}(M;Z) is trivial if M is orientable and Z2 if M is nonorientable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the universal coefficient theorem and considerations of H_n(M;Z_p) for primes p; the Z2 in the nonorientable case is identified as the image of the Bockstein H_n(M;Z2)→H_{n-1}(M;Z) coming from 0→Z→Z→Z2→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3.29: homology of noncompact manifolds vanishes in top dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a connected noncompact n-manifold, then H_i(M;R) = 0 for i ≥ n (coefficients R a ring as in context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: represent classes by cycles with compact image; use complements of compact sets and long exact sequences plus local homology vanishing (Lemma 3.27) to show cycles are boundaries. For i=n an argument using sections of the orientation local system shows vanishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic property of cap product
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap product a: C_k(X;R) × C^ℓ(X;R) → C_{k−ℓ}(X;R) for k ≥ ℓ is defined by splitting a simplex and evaluating the cochain on the front face; it satisfies ∂(σ a ϕ) = (−1)^ℓ(∂σ a ϕ − σ a δϕ), so it induces a bilinear cap product H_k × H^ℓ → H_{k−ℓ} and has natural relative versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the explicit formula and the boundary relation used to check well-definedness on homology/cohomology; relative and naturality properties are discussed, including relative cap products H_k(X,A;R)×H^ℓ(X;R)→H_{k−ℓ}(X,A;R) and more general relative forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of cap product with respect to maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f:X→Y, the cap product satisfies f_*(α) a ϕ = f_*(α a f^*(ϕ)) (formula as stated in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This naturality mixes covariant and contravariant functors; one checks by substituting fσ for σ in the definition. Relative versions hold as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.30 (Poincaré Duality for closed orientable manifolds)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a closed R-orientable n-manifold with fundamental class [M] ∈ H_n(M;R), then the map D: H^k(M;R) → H_{n−k}(M;R) defined by D(α) = [M] a α is an isomorphism for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires existence of fundamental class (constructed earlier). The statement is the classic Poincaré duality for closed orientable manifolds, realized via cap product with [M].

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicial computation guidance / example for surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For closed orientable surfaces (genus g) one can compute cap products simplicially; fundamental class represented by sum of oriented 2-simplices with signs; cohomology classes α_i, β_i dual to loops a_i, b_i satisfy [M] a ϕ_i = b_i, [M] a ψ_i = −a_i, showing Poincaré duality exchanges those generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative example: how to compute cap products in practice using simplicial cycles and cocycles; indicates geometric interpretation of duality (loops homotopic to their duals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: singular cohomology with compact supports
rubrics_metrics.description: C^i_c(X;G) is the subgroup of singular cochains ϕ: C_i(X)→G for which there exists a compact set K⊂X so that ϕ vanishes on all chains in X−K; its cohomology H^i_c(X;G) is cohomology with compact supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes the definition is weaker than requiring support contained in a compact set of singular simplices; explains alternative description via direct limits: H^i_c(X;G) ≅ lim_{K compact} H^i(X,X−K;G). Examples: H^1_c(R;G) ≅ G, H^n_c(R^n;G) ≅ G, others zero. Proper maps induce maps on H^*_c, and H^*_c is not a homotopy invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3.33: direct limit description for unions of directed subspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is the union of a directed set of subspaces X_α with the property that each compact set in X is contained in some X_α, then the natural map lim_{→} H_i(X_α;G) → H_i(X;G) is an isomorphism for all i and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surjectivity via representing cycles by finitely many simplices (compact image), injectivity by compactness of boundaries; used to identify cohomology with compact supports as the direct limit over compact subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative description of H^i_c via direct limits
rubrics_metrics.description: H^i_c(X;G) = lim_{→, K compact} H^i(X, X−K; G); equivalently H^i_c is the limit over compact subsets of local cohomology groups H^i(X || K;G) = H^i(X, X−K;G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why direct limit equals compactly supported cohomology: each compactly supported cocycle lives in some H^i(X, X−K;G), and being null in the limit corresponds to being a coboundary after enlarging K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.35: Poincaré duality for R-orientable (possibly noncompact) n-manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: For M an R-orientable n-manifold (possibly noncompact), the duality map D_M: H^k_c(M;R) → H_{n−k}(M;R) obtained by taking limits of local cap products is an isomorphism for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: (i) establish a Mayer–Vietoris lemma (Lemma 3.36) for compact-support sequences commuting up to sign, (ii) two inductive steps A (finite Mayer–Vietoris) and B (direct limit over increasing union of opens), and (iii) finish via Zorn's Lemma to extend from R^n-charts to whole manifold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.36: Mayer–Vietoris for compactly supported cohomology and duality diagram commutativity
rubrics_metrics.description: If M = U ∪ V (open), then there is a diagram of Mayer–Vietoris sequences (for homology and compactly supported cohomology) which is commutative up to sign; passing to direct limits over compact subsets yields the Mayer–Vietoris sequence used in the duality proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical proof analyzes the square involving coboundary and boundary maps, represents orientation classes µ_K by chains decomposed across U−L, U∩V, V−K, and checks commutativity up to sign using cap product identities and support vanishing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.37: Euler characteristic of odd-dimensional closed manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed manifold of odd dimension has Euler characteristic zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use Poincaré duality to pair ranks/dimensions of H^i and H^{n−i} (or Z2-coefficients if nonorientable) so alternating sum cancels; treat torsion contributions carefully via universal coefficient theorem and Z2 reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection formula between cup and cap products
rubrics_metrics.description: For α ∈ C_{k+ℓ}(X;R), ϕ ∈ C^k(X;R), ψ ∈ C^ℓ(X;R) one has ψ(α a ϕ) = (ϕ ∪ ψ)(α). Equivalently, the map ϕ∪: C^ℓ→C^{k+ℓ} is dual to a_ϕ: C_{k+ℓ}→C_ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identity implies that under hypotheses (e.g. R a field or H_* free and finitely generated) cup and cap determine each other via duality; but torsion can obstruct equivalence when R=Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3.38: nonsingularity of cup product pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed R-orientable manifold M, the cup product pairing H^k(M;R) × H^{n−k}(M;R) → R, (ϕ,ψ) ↦ (ϕ ∪ ψ)[M], is nonsingular when R is a field or when R = Z and torsion in H^*(M;Z) is factored out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof composes the universal coefficient evaluation map h with the dual of Poincaré duality; nonsingularity in each variable follows when h and D are isomorphisms. This yields strong algebraic constraints on cup product structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.39: detection of Z-summands via cup product
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is closed connected orientable n-manifold, α ∈ H^k(M;Z) generates an infinite cyclic summand of H^k(M;Z) iff there exists β ∈ H^{n−k}(M;Z) with α ∪ β a generator of H^n(M;Z) ≈ Z. Over a field, any nonzero α has such a β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses nonsingularity of the cup pairing: a homomorphism H^k→Z with value ±1 on α is realized by cup product with β and evaluation on [M].

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle-dimensional cup product form on H^n_free(M) for 2n-manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed orientable 2n-manifold M, the middle-dimensional cup product induces a nonsingular bilinear form on H^n_free(M) which is symmetric if n is even and skew-symmetric if n is odd; in particular the rank of H^n(M) is even when n is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic classification remarks: skew-symmetric nonsingular forms over Z can be put in standard 2×2 block form; symmetric integral forms are more intricate and have finitely many isomorphism classes for fixed rank (applications to 4k-manifolds and classification notes given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and computational guidance (projective and lens spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples compute cup and cap product structures: H^*(CP^n;Z) ≅ Z[α]/(α^{n+1}) with |α|=2, H^*(HP^n;Z) ≅ Z[α]/(α^{n+1}) with |α|=4, H^*(RP^n;Z2) ≅ Z2[α]/(α^{n+1}) with |α|=1. For lens spaces L^{2n+1} with fundamental group Z_m, explicit generators α∈H^1, β∈H^2 and relations determine all homology and cup products (with parity/m divisibility conditions explained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how to apply duality and universal coefficient arguments to determine ring structures; includes notes on how torsion and parity affect cup squares (α^2) and top-dimensional generators.
